task1.title: Online shopping in Australia by age group, 2007 and 2009
task1.prompt: The bar chart below shows the percentage of people in Australia who shopped online in different age groups in 2007 and 2009.

chartDesc.title: People in Australia who shopped online by age group
chartDesc.overview: Online shopping increased across all age groups in Australia from 2007 to 2009. The 26-35 age group had the highest percentage of online shoppers in both years, whereas the 65+ age group recorded the lowest percentage.
keyFeatures: The 26-35 age group was the highest in both years, rising from 38% in 2007 to 43% in 2009.
The lowest proportions were among people aged 65+, standing at 10% in 2007 and 12% in 2009.
The overall average percentage of people who shopped online increased from 24% in 2007 to 29% in 2009.
The largest increases occurred in the 26-35, 46-55, and 56-65 age categories, each rising by 5 percentage points.

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
task1.sampleBand8:
The bar chart shows what percentage of Australians in six age groups bought goods online in 2007 and 2009, together with the national average.

Overall, online shopping grew across the board over the two years, with the average rising from 24% to 29%. In both years, participation peaked among 26–35-year-olds and then fell progressively with age, so the oldest shoppers were consistently the least active online.

The 26–35 group led the way by a clear margin, with 38% shopping online in 2007 and 43% in 2009 — well above the average in both years. They were followed by 36–45-year-olds, whose figure rose from 30% to 34%, and by the 46–55 group, which recorded one of the larger increases, from 23% to 28%.

At the two ends of the age range, activity was more limited. Only a fifth of the youngest shoppers, aged 15–25, bought online in 2007, and this edged up just two points to 22%. The 56–65 group climbed more markedly, from 15% to 20%, while people aged 65 and over remained the least likely to shop online, at 10% rising to 12%. It is noteworthy that every single group grew, yet the overall ranking of the age groups was unchanged between the two years.
task1.uzSampleBand8:
Ustunli diagramma 2007 va 2009-yillarda olti yosh guruhidagi avstraliyaliklarning necha foizi internet orqali xarid qilganini hamda umumiy o'rtacha ko'rsatkichni aks ettiradi.

Umuman olganda, ikki yil ichida onlayn xaridlar barcha guruhlarda o'sdi va o'rtacha ko'rsatkich 24 foizdan 29 foizga ko'tarildi. Har ikkala yilda ham ishtirok 26–35 yoshlilar orasida eng yuqori cho'qqiga chiqqan va keyin yosh oshgan sari izchil pasayib borgan, shu bois eng keksa xaridorlar internetda doimiy ravishda eng sust bo'lgan.

26–35 yoshlilar guruhi yaqqol ustunlik bilan yetakchilik qildi: 2007-yilda ularning 38 foizi, 2009-yilda esa 43 foizi onlayn xarid qilgan — bu har ikkala yilda ham o'rtachadan ancha yuqori. Ulardan keyin ko'rsatkichi 30 dan 34 foizga o'sgan 36–45 yoshlilar hamda eng katta o'sishlardan birini — 23 dan 28 foizgacha — qayd etgan 46–55 guruh turadi.

Yosh oralig'ining ikki chekkasida faollik cheklangan edi. 15–25 yoshli eng yosh xaridorlarning atigi beshdan biri 2007-yilda onlayn xarid qilgan va bu ko'rsatkich bor-yo'g'i ikki bandga, 22 foizga sal ko'tarildi. 56–65 guruh ancha sezilarli — 15 dan 20 foizgacha — o'sdi, 65 va undan katta yoshdagilar esa 10 foizdan 12 foizga ko'tarilgan holda onlayn xarid qilish ehtimoli eng past guruh bo'lib qoldi. Shunisi diqqatga sazovorki, har bir guruh o'sgan bo'lsa-da, yosh guruhlarining umumiy tartibi ikki yil orasida o'zgarmadi.

task2.title: Is money the most important motivator at work?
task2.prompt: Many factors motivate people in the workplace. Some people think money is the most important factor. Do you agree or disagree?
task2.instruction: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
task2.sampleBand8:
What drives people to work hard is a perennial question for employers, and many assume that a bigger salary is the answer. While I agree that money is a powerful incentive, I disagree that it is the most important one, because other factors sustain motivation far more reliably.

The importance of pay is undeniable. Most people work primarily to make a living, and a salary that fails to cover housing, food and family expenses makes every other aspect of a job irrelevant. Financial rewards such as bonuses also produce quick, measurable bursts of effort, which is precisely why companies use them; a fair wage further signals that an employer values its staff, protecting morale.

Nevertheless, money's power fades once basic needs are met. Psychologists studying workplace behaviour have repeatedly found that pay rises deliver only a short-lived boost, whereas job satisfaction — feeling that one's work is meaningful and appreciated — keeps people engaged for years. Factors such as recognition from managers, genuine career prospects, a healthy work-life balance and a friendly team explain why many professionals stay in modestly paid jobs they love, and why others leave lucrative positions they find soul-destroying. High-paying firms with toxic cultures still suffer constant staff turnover, which shows that salary alone cannot buy commitment.

In conclusion, although money matters greatly, particularly for those on low incomes, I believe it is not the single most important motivator. Once pay is adequate, it is purpose, recognition and working conditions that truly determine how motivated people are.
task2.uzSampleBand8:
Odamlarni mehnatga nima undashi ish beruvchilar uchun doimiy savol bo'lib, ko'pchilik javob kattaroq maoshda deb o'ylaydi. Pul kuchli rag'bat ekaniga qo'shilsam-da, u eng muhimi degan fikrga qo'shilmayman, chunki boshqa omillar ishtiyoqni ancha barqarorroq saqlab turadi.

Maoshning ahamiyati shubhasiz. Aksariyat odamlar birinchi navbatda kun kechirish uchun ishlaydi va uy-joy, oziq-ovqat hamda oila xarajatlarini qoplamaydigan maosh ishning boshqa barcha jihatlarini ma'nosiz qilib qo'yadi. Bonus kabi moddiy mukofotlar ham tez va o'lchanadigan g'ayrat portlashlarini beradi — kompaniyalar ulardan aynan shu sababli foydalanadi; adolatli maosh esa ish beruvchi xodimlarini qadrlashini bildirib, ruhiyatni himoya qiladi.

Shunga qaramay, asosiy ehtiyojlar qondirilgach, pulning kuchi so'na boradi. Ish joyidagi xulq-atvorni o'rganuvchi psixologlar maosh oshirish faqat qisqa muddatli ko'tarilish berishini qayta-qayta aniqlashgan, ishdan qoniqish — mehnati mazmunli va e'tirof etilayotganini his qilish — esa odamlarni yillar davomida ishtiyoqli saqlaydi. Rahbarlarning e'tirofi, chinakam martaba istiqbollari, sog'lom ish va hayot muvozanati hamda ahil jamoa kabi omillar nega ko'plab mutaxassislar o'zlari sevgan kamtarona maoshli ishlarda qolishini, boshqalar esa ruhni ezadigan serdaromad lavozimlarni tark etishini izohlaydi. Zaharli muhitli yuqori maoshli firmalar baribir doimiy kadrlar almashinuvidan aziyat chekadi — bu maoshning o'zi sadoqatni sotib ola olmasligini ko'rsatadi.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, pul, ayniqsa kam daromadlilar uchun, juda muhim bo'lsa-da, u yagona eng muhim rag'bat emas deb hisoblayman. Maosh yetarli bo'lgach, odamlarning ishtiyoqini aslida maqsad, e'tirof va mehnat sharoitlari belgilaydi.
